To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the agents in the Internet can be modeled as autonomous, adaptive, and trustworthy.

the agents can cooperate in order to improve the performance of the overall system, that the agents can learn to adaptively select their service providers in order to obtain better quality services, and that the agents can use the quality information they collect to help other agents find better service providers.
An agent-based approach for trustworthy service location can provide better service location than traditional approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an agent-based approach to service location.
the following questions: How can we model the Internet as a distributed information system whose components are autonomous agents?
the following questions: 1) how to build an index for a service, 2) how to select a service provider, and 3) how to adapt to the changing environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Internet is a peer-to-peer system that supports a decentralized index and that is based upon a trust-based service location mechanism that allows the agents to adapt to their changing environment.
there is no evidence to support the hypothesis that the Internet is a global brain, but that it is possible that it could be one.
the Internet is a peer-to-peer service network whose components are agents that can cooperate with one other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an approach to service discovery in which agents maintain local indexes of services and use them to select neighbors.
we have developed a framework to model service discovery in a distributed system of autonomous agents and have shown that this framework can be implemented in a practical manner.
we have proposed a novel approach that allows agents to dynamically select their neighbors based on their performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the web could be made more trustworthy by having agents cooperate to find the best service providers.
a peer-to-peer approach can provide a more robust and flexible service location infrastructure than centralized approaches.
a peer-to-peer system can be built in a decentralized fashion, without the need for centralized indexing, and without requiring agents to have global information about the system.
